Senses.PreferredTarget: register and take a monastic place
AlternateTargets: take an assigned place in the monks’ hall
Senses.Explanation: The graphs mean “hang” and “attach,” but Chan institutional records use the compound for registering and taking an assigned place in a monastery. The Chan Monastic Regulations gives the procedure: a new arrival who wishes to register waits a day or two, presents himself at the hall office with his ordination document, and requests residence. After registration he stores his luggage, hangs his bowl, and arranges his bedding in the monks’ hall. The Baizhang Monastic Regulations states the older order more compactly: one seeking residence first presents himself at the guest office, then registers at the hall office, after which his assigned place is settled. When the abbot permits registration, the attendant’s office issues a notice to the hall office, tea and the bed register follow, and the newcomer is sent into the common quarters. Recorded sayings use the same institutional verb: one teacher tells two determined visitors, “You two want to investigate Chan; go register,” while another newcomer is told to register elsewhere until a place becomes vacant and he can enter the hall.
Senses.Note: The headword occurs 145 times in 38 allowlisted texts. The regulations distinguish seeking registration, the abbot permitting it, new registrants, greater and lesser registration procedures, returning to the hall, tea for new registrants, and thanks after registration. “Seek registration” occurs 8 times in 4 texts; “permit registration” occurs twice in two. The corpus therefore supplies a concrete lodging-and-admission procedure. In some biographies the completed verb simply marks that a traveler resided at the named monastery.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若欲掛搭。歇一兩日。詣堂司相看。掛搭掛搭具威儀。袖祠部。於堂司相看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chan Monastic Regulations, section on temporary lodging: one who wishes to register waits one or two days, then formally presents himself at the hall office carrying his ordination document.

Occurrences.Kwic: 掛搭了。如堂中有函櫃。即收行李安函櫃中鏁之。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Chan Monastic Regulations, section on packing: after registration, luggage is placed in a hall cabinet and locked; the following instructions place bowl and bedding in the monks’ hall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 依棲求掛搭古規首到客司相看。次往堂司掛搭。送單位經案定。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Revised Baizhang Monastic Regulations, section on traveling for inquiry: under the old rule, one seeking residence first presents himself at the guest office, then registers at the hall office, and has his assigned place settled.

Occurrences.Kwic: 方丈許掛搭。侍司發榜下堂司。請茶上床曆畢。送入眾寮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Baizhang regulations describe permission and admission: the abbot permits registration, the attendant’s office sends notice to the hall office, tea and the bed register are completed, and the person is sent into the common quarters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 你兩箇要參禪，却去掛搭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Pujue Zonggao, biographical preface: after two visitors refuse to leave even under threat of a beating, the teacher laughs and says, “You two want to investigate Chan; go register.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 且令別處掛搭，候此間單位空，即令入堂。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The same preface records a vacancy decision: “For now let him register elsewhere; when a single place here is vacant, let him enter the hall.”
